description:
GOAL: Add the built-in File runtime-library module as the first client of the shared resource lifecycle, so fz programs can perform a practical Elixir-shaped filesystem surface directly through C externs.

SIGNAL:
- The real runtime File module is lazy-loadable from the bootstrap registry.
- File owns an opaque resource handle and uses the generic guarded-use and one-shot disposal contract.
- A behavior fixture exercises direct-C create, write, read, append, open, close, link, directory, and failure paths across interp, run, and build.
- No File-specific Rust filesystem bridge exists; Rust owns only generic resource safety.
- Rust and fixture gates pass with no new warnings.

STRATEGY:
1. Inventory ../elixir/lib/elixir/lib/file.ex against fz capabilities and document accurate supported surface/divergences.
2. Declare private libc symbols in lib/file.fz and translate their return values in fz source.
3. Use the resource lifecycle primitives for handles, guarded IO, and deterministic close.
4. Replace temporary fixture-local File names with the built-in module and pin cross-door behavior.
5. Document the public contract, including shared-handle close semantics and unsupported Elixir features.
title: Runtime library: add File surface
